claim: In practice the 15 house bots act as one squad that never fights each other and sends hunters at us one at a time early (weakest first), so practice placement points come only from our kills and house-bot zone deaths before we die.

sources.quote: acting as one squad: they share vision, never fight each other, and hunt you weakest first (one early, more as you thin them out, all of them late)
Premise "house bots never kill each other" unverified

suggested_change: Treat the first lone hunter as a fight to win, not a threat to flee: while exactly one enemy mech is known, skip the 35% HP retreat unless the TTK/TTD test in the next finding says we lose.
mechanism: With no house-vs-house kills, the RCA's 62/65 public-match infighting does not carry over to practice. Outlasting earns only zone deaths, and the house squad stays in the zone, so each of our kills is close to one placement point. The early hunters are one at a time and of the weakest tier, which is the cheapest time to bank kills before the squad converges.

failure_classes.basis: retreat triggers on our HP alone (brain.ts:359,365) even against a single, weak, wounded hunter
fleeing a lone hunter lets more hunters arrive later (track page: more as you thin them out)

author: Diego

claim: Everything needed for a time-to-kill vs time-to-die test is in the observation: visible mechs carry hp, max_hp, cubes, weapons and charging, and the kit config sets vision.show_enemy_hp true. brain.ts already stores Known.hp and hpLog but never reads them.

sources.quote: `hp` is shown while `vision.show_enemy_hp` is true
"show_enemy_hp": true
k.hpLog.push([obs.t, k.hp])

suggested_change: Compute ttk = enemy.hp / (our DPS for the weapon in hand x hit rate) and ttd = our hp / (sum of DPS of enemies with LOS to us, by their observed weapons); fight when ttk < params.aggression x ttd, else retreat. params.aggression already exists and is unread.
mechanism: Replaces 'flee at 35% HP' with a decision that depends on the enemy's HP and weapons, so we stop turning away from targets we would finish first.

failure_classes.basis: RCA Q1/Q5: no TTK estimate exists; aggression param unread (params.ts:17)

author: Diego

claim: Weapon damage rates from the kit config: gun 45 dmg every 0.24 s is 187.5 DPS in a burst and about 102 DPS sustained (12 rounds = 540 dmg per 2.88 s + 2.4 s reload); laser 315 per full shot with a 0.75 s charge + 1.65 s cooldown is about 131 DPS, hitscan; lightning 60 every 0.25 s is 240 DPS inside 45 m for about 8 s on 100 energy (3 per shot, 18/s regen). A 1400 HP mech needs 32 gun hits (about 12.5 s at perfect accuracy) or 5 full laser shots.

sources.quote: "gun": {"damage": 45, "cooldown": 0.24, ... "mag": 12, "reload": 2.4}

sources.ref: mechfight-kit/protocol.md §7 Weapons table (gun, laser, lightning rows)

suggested_change: Seed the TTK/TTD test with these per-weapon DPS values read from hello.config at hello (never hard-coded), times a hit-rate guess of 0.5 for the gun beyond 60 m and 0.9 for laser and lightning.
mechanism: At 35% HP (490 HP) we die to 11 gun hits (about 2.6 s of burst) while backing away; an enemy at <=540 HP dies to one of our gun magazines in 2.9 s. Many current retreats therefore give up a nearly won fight and still take the hits.

failure_classes.basis: arithmetic from config; no per-match data on our own fights

author: Diego

claim: Finishing a wounded enemy pays twice: each kill is roughly a placement point in practice and drops all of its cubes plus 2, which reaches the first upgrade thresholds (1 and 3 cubes) from a single kill.

sources.quote: Killed mechs drop all their cubes plus two.
% of mech hits on targets under 50% HP: winner 46.6 top4 37.1 bottom 24.7

suggested_change: Always commit (no retreat, keep firing, walk to collect the death drop) when the target's hp is at most one magazine of our current weapon (gun 540 x cube damage mult, laser 315) and no second enemy has LOS to us.
mechanism: Converts near-kills we currently abandon at 35% HP into a point plus 2+ cubes (+8% HP and damage and an upgrade offer), which also feeds Build 12 FARM.

failure_classes.basis: target choice is nearest-clear, never lowest-HP (brain.ts:408-419)
death drops are only picked up by chance today

author: Diego

claim: Both observations are true because they describe different match modes: the track rules say practice house bots act as one squad and never fight each other, while the 62-of-65 house-on-house kills were measured in public play.joinbuilders.org matches (humans plus house bots). Nothing in the kit says the two modes share house-bot behavior. Public-match infighting is therefore no evidence about practice, and practice placement points come only from our kills and house zone deaths.

sources.quote: acting as one squad: they share vision, never fight each other
62 of 65 house-bot deaths were kills by other house bots ... MEASURED (public matches only. Practice house config is unverified.)
played in 48 practice matches against built-in bots

suggested_change: For practice and qualifying-for-top-32 work, plan on fighting: take winnable 1v1s against the early lone hunters and finish wounded targets (EV-R-0020..0023). Don't tune hiding or outlasting on practice. Revisit hiding only for the final, where the track page says the qualifying round and the series are 16-mech free-for-alls between team bots, which do kill each other.
mechanism: If no house bot ever kills another, a 48-match practice score of 2.38 means about 2.4 squad deaths before ours, from our kills or the zone. Hiding only delays our death against a squad that shares vision and adds hunters over time, so it cannot add places. Kills add places directly and drop cubes.

failure_classes.basis: practice rules: placement only from our kills and zone deaths; the bot flees at 35% of its own HP regardless of the enemy

author: Diego

claim: Outside an engagement latch, brain.ts shoots the nearest clear enemy, not the one it would kill fastest, even though Build 14 already computes per-enemy time-to-kill (race()).

sources.quote: // Target: the nearest enemy mech with a clear shot, else the nearest one we know is there.
return { ttk: out > 0 ? e.hp! / out : Infinity, ttd: taken > 0 ? me.hp / taken : Infinity }
% of mech hits on targets under 50% HP: winner 46.6 top4 37.1 bottom 24.7

suggested_change: Next build (one mechanism, brain.ts target sort at :651): among clear targets, after the engaged-target tiebreak, sort by ttk from race() (enemy hp / ourDps at its distance) instead of distance; fall back to distance on ties or when hp is missing. Behind a flag (e.g. TARGET_TTK_ON) so it rolls back to Build 14 exactly. Expected: +0.1 to +0.3, more kills, because the squad converges late (more targets at once) and split damage across full-HP hunters kills nobody.
mechanism: In practice every point is a squad death before ours. With two or more hunters in view, concentrating fire on the one closest to dying turns damage into kills (each worth about a point and its cubes + 2) before the squad's damage turns into our death. The finish rule only covers the engaged target; this applies the same idea to every shot.

failure_classes.basis: damage spread over full-HP enemies yields no kill
late-match squad convergence: several hunters in view at once (track rules)

author: Diego

claim: While the laser leads, the torso aims straight at the target with no lead, so the gun's onTarget(gunAim) check fails against a sideways mover beyond about 65 m and the gun stays silent for the whole 0.75 s charge.

sources.quote:
leading = "laser"
          aim = direct

sources.ref: mechfight-kit/check/stream.jsonl.gz hello.config (gun speed 252, mech radius 2.5, walk_speed 11.7, laser charge 0.75, cooldown 1.65)

suggested_change: When both laser and gun are held, fire the gun with the laser's direct aim when the lead offset (sideways speed x d / gun speed) is under the target radius, and otherwise aim at gunAim during the charge and release the laser only when |aim - direct| is within yawTol. Candidate for after the target-choice build.
mechanism: The lead a sideways mover needs at walk speed is 11.7 x d / 252 = 0.046 x d m. That passes the 3 m tolerance (radius 2.5 x 1.2) at about 65 m. The charge is 0.75 of each 2.4 s laser cycle, so about 31% of the time the gun (about 102 DPS sustained) is silenced against moving targets at mid range. This may be part of why Build 8 (laser first) lost: a laser can replace gun DPS instead of adding to it.

failure_classes.basis: code reading plus arithmetic from config, no per-match data

author: Diego

claim: A started laser charge keeps charging when the target loses line of sight or the laser stops leading, so it auto-fires after hold_s (2 s past full charge) along whatever the torso faces and then spends its 1.65 s cooldown.

sources.quote: fire[laser] = !(full && leading === "laser" && onTarget(direct[0], direct[1]))
a full charge held for `hold_s` 2 s more fires on its own

suggested_change: When charging and the target is no longer clear or in range, release only if it is on target; otherwise keep the charge and re-aim at the nearest clear enemy before the hold_s auto-fire. Small fix, can ride with the laser-aim change.
mechanism: A wasted full charge throws away 315 damage plus 2.4 s of laser cycle, and charging also halves our walk speed (charge_move_mult 0.5) while it lasts, during retreats too.

failure_classes.basis: code reading; frequency unknown without match data

author: Diego

claim: Build 8's laser-seek rule could start a trip at spawn in at most 12-16% of real spawns (19/160 public, 35/224 showdown), because it only knows lasers visible this tick without turning and keeps the 160 m enemy gate; a ground laser is in the spawn view wedge without turning in 28-29% of spawns.

sources.quote: if (!enemies.some((m) => flat(m.pos, me.pos) < LOOT_CLEAR))

suggested_change: Do not retry laser-first with a see-it-now rule; add a spawn scan and pickup memory first (see ARM-UP finding).
mechanism: A build that changes behaviour in about one spawn in seven cannot move the laser-by-30-s rate toward the winners' 71%, while its aim changes applied in every laser match.
author: Doug

claim: Showdown winners who hold a laser by 30 s (10 of 14) got it from the floor (7, of which 6 were the nearest laser to spawn) or from a crate they shot (3), never from a roof, after walking a median 78 m (straight line median 58 m, max 176 m), and 9 of 10 of those trips had an enemy inside 160 m at some point.

sources.quote: trip with an enemy inside 160 m at some point | 90% (9/10)

suggested_change: ARM-UP build: spawn scan plus 60 s pickup memory plus a nav walk to the best remembered ground laser or lightning within about 175 m while gun-only, with no 160 m enemy gate (stop only when a mech is hitting us or the zone test fails).
mechanism: After a full turn a ground laser or lightning is visible within 130 m from 58-59% of spawns and within 175 m from 65%, against 12-16% for Build 8's rule. In first engagements, laser against no laser is 14 kills and 2 deaths in 30; the reverse is 5 kills and 16 deaths in 44.

failure_classes.basis: most matches are fought gun-only; winners are 14/14 with a laser

author: Doug

claim: The Wolverines bot (rank 3 on the 9:40 PM board) spins its torso for the first 3 s, sweeps around its heading while walking, remembers ground pickups for 60 s, and walks to the best remembered weapon with no distance cap and no enemy-distance gate outside fight mode.

sources.quote: if (t < 3) aimYaw = me.aim[0] + 1.6
this.pickMem.set(p.id, { pos: p.pos, kind: p.kind, t })

suggested_change: Same ARM-UP build: scan at spawn, remember pickups, drop the 80 m detour and 160 m gate while gun-only.
mechanism: Pickups are listed only while seen (protocol.md:374), so a bot that neither turns nor remembers knows a small share of the weapons near it.
author: Doug

claim: Quiet slow-walking costs points in practice for other teams: the same Lance controller scored 4.54 with its 4.6 m/s sneak cap on and 4.75 with it off, and r1ver went from 4.54 to 4.67 with normal speed plus a supply-capture fix.

sources.quote: explicit MR_FLAGS empty; quiet speed cap disabled ... 4.75
practice: squad focus-fire makes cover-seek too passive; FFA only

suggested_change: STOP SNEAKING build: remove the silent speed cap (brain.ts:417, :629-630) and the hide-from-sight move (brain.ts:619-625) while not hurt, behind one flag.
mechanism: The house squad shares vision and hunts the weakest, so creeping and hiding delay farming, arming and first shots without preventing contact.

failure_classes.basis: bot creeps under 5 m/s inside the next circle and walks to hiding spots when seen at full HP

author: Doug

claim: House bots in public matches hit far less often than Build 14 assumes: gun 64-83% at 30-60 m, 26-57% at 60-100 m, 10-35% at 100-150 m, 2-13% at 150-230 m; laser 15-27% overall. Build 14 assumes 80% inside 60 m, 50% beyond, and 90% for lasers.

sources.quote: const HIT_GUN_NEAR = 0.8 / const HIT_GUN_FAR = 0.5 / const HIT_BEAM = 0.9

suggested_change: CALIBRATED RACE build: replace the enemy-side hit-rate constants with a by-range table from these measurements, and hold a weapon standoff (110 m with a laser, about 80 m gun-only) instead of closing to 60 m.
mechanism: ttd is underestimated by 1.5-5x beyond 60 m, so the TTK rule rarely fires (coord/log.md:239) and the finish rule closes to the range where house guns are most accurate.
author: Doug

claim: Showdown lasers keep their hit rate with range (49-89% in every bin from 30 to 230 m; winners 57-84%) while showdown guns fall from 82-95% at 30-60 m to 25-37% at 150-230 m, and every group fires the laser at full charge (median 0.80 s).
suggested_change: With a laser in hand, fight at 100-200 m rather than closing; release only at full charge.
mechanism: At 100-230 m a laser at about 131 DPS times a 70% hit rate out-damages a gun at 102 DPS times 25-50%, and house guns hit 2-35% there.
author: Doug

claim: Our laser releases with up to 3.0 m of sideways aim error (4.2 m at 280 m) against a mech of radius 2.5 m, because yawTol is atan2(radius x size x 1.2, d) with a 0.015 rad floor; the Wolverines bot releases inside 0.9 x a 2.2 m half-width.

sources.quote: const yawTol = Math.max(0.015, Math.atan2(cfg.mech.radius * size * 1.2, d))
A mech is a vertical cylinder of radius 2.5 m and height 9 m
yawErr < tol * 0.9

suggested_change: Give the laser release its own yaw tolerance of at most 0.8 x the target radius (no 0.015 rad floor).
mechanism: A beam released between 2.5 m and 3.0 m off the target axis misses, then costs a 1.65 s cooldown.

failure_classes.basis: release tolerance wider than the target

author: Doug

claim: In showdown first engagements the winner of the match landed the first hit 79% of the time (bottom half 47%); pooled, landing the first hit gives 42 kills and 23 deaths in 119, taking it gives 16 kills and 34 deaths in 103, and having someone else also hitting you gives 26 deaths in 40. Lateral speed does not differ (6.1 vs 6.4 m/s).

sources.quote: first hit mine: n=119 KILL=42 DIED=23 ... first hit theirs: n=103 KILL=16 DIED=34

suggested_change: Open fire on first clear sight inside effective range instead of moving to a hiding spot first; do not spend a build on strafing.
mechanism: The side that starts the damage race ahead wins it more than twice as often.
author: Doug

claim: By protocol values gun_mag is the largest single damage upgrade for a gun fight (sustained gun DPS 102.3 to 133.9, +31%), ahead of laser_damage (+18%), plating (+15% HP) and gun_damage (+15%); sensors adds nothing to a fight yet ranks above every weapon upgrade in our order, and all weapon upgrades tie.

sources.quote: gun_mag: +8 rounds, -20% reload time
const UPGRADE_FIRST = ["plating", "armor", "nanites", "sensors"]

suggested_change: Keep plating > armor > nanites, then rank weapon upgrades gun_mag, laser_damage, gun_damage, laser_charge, gun_rate, lightning_efficiency, and move sensors below them.
mechanism: A 1,400 HP target needs several magazines at real hit rates, so reload time dominates gun DPS.
